Subject: Renewal: phased top-up + co-term path for Navisys

Elena —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Attached is an updated renewal packet with two practical paths we discussed: a) a phased top-up with volume bands and capped surcharges to bridge current overage risk, and b) a straight co-term with an annualized uplift. Key points in the PDF: 

- Phased top-up: 3-month bridge to smooth billing + 2-tier surcharge cap (5% / 10%) if usage spikes beyond agreed bands.
- Volume bands: lower unit price for confirmed commit bands, step-up pricing for higher usage.
- Co-term option: annualize remaining quarter into a single co-term invoice with a one-time 7% uplift.
- Credit: we can apply a $25k adoption voucher if you sign the co-term before Dec 15.

I also attached an editable SOW with the updated seats + throughput targets.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You let us know preferred path (phased top-up vs co-term)
2) If phased top-up, confirm which band (Base+20% or Base+40%) we should provision for provisional capacity
3) If co-term, we’ll prepare DocuSign and a single combined invoice for procurement.

Ben and Lauren are looped for pricing flexibility and invoicing cadence. Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks,

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Appreciate the options and the clear summary. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and engineering: 

1) On the phased top-up, how are surcharges calculated? Is it per-token or per-GB of processed input? Engineering wants predictable per-request economics.
2) For the volume bands, can we get an escalation clause if usage stays above the top band for two consecutive months?
3) If we opt for the co-term and take the $25k voucher, are there any usage floors or minimums we need to commit to?

We’re aiming to present to the finance committee next Tuesday (Nov 24). If you can get back with answers + a net-new quote by EOD Monday that would be ideal.

Also, procurement would prefer separate line items for licenses, support, and infra credits for transparency on the PO.

—Elena

Elena — looping in Marissa (legal) and Lauren (billing). Quick answers while we prep the formal quote: 

- Surcharges: calculated as a % uplift on the per-token rate and only apply to incremental usage beyond the band. They are applied monthly and capped per month as noted (5% cap for band A, 10% cap for band B). That keeps per-request costs stable for the committed portion.
- Escalation clause: yes — we can add a consecutive-month clause: after two months above the top band, we trigger a re-evaluation call and offer an automatic 10% one-time credit if you move to the next committed band within 30 days.
- Voucher / floors: the $25k voucher is independent of a usage floor, but co-term commit requires a 12-month minimum billing estimate (simple annualized commit) to qualify. We will make that explicit on the quote line items.

Marissa — can you confirm the clause language for the consecutive-month escalation and the voucher T&Cs? Lauren — once we have the final band selection I’ll request a split invoice: license, support, infra credit.

Ben

Elena / team —

Draft language for the two items below (happy to iterate):

1) Consecutive-Month Escalation Clause (draft): 
"If Customer’s billable usage exceeds the top volume band for two consecutive billing cycles, Redwood and Customer will meet within ten (10) business days to evaluate capacity requirements. If Customer elects to commit to the next volume band within thirty (30) days of the meeting, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 10% of the net incremental commit for the remainder of the then-current term."

2) Voucher Terms (draft): 
"The $25,000 adoption voucher is a one-time, non-transferable credit applied to the Customer’s Redwood invoice upon execution of the co-term amendment before the stated deadline. The voucher may be applied to subscription and usage charges, excluding taxes and third-party pass-throughs. Voucher does not require a minimum usage floor but requires a signed amendment committing to the 12‑month co-term annualized estimate."

Comments: legal prefers not to have open-ended automatic credits; the re-eval + conditional credit keeps the incentive aligned.

If procurement wants the voucher in a separate invoice line item for visibility, Lauren can do that.

Marissa Cole
